You are extracting a TESTABLE RUBRIC from three front-end engineering documents. Read each one IN FULL — do not skim or sample. They are moderate size (763, 807 and 792 lines).

2. /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/fedBuild-manual.md
3. /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/fedLead-playbook.md

CONTEXT
These describe how UI should be built in a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (Zimmermann, Chakra UI, TypeScript, an `overrides/` customisation layer over `@salesforce/retail-react-app`). They were revised 2026-08-25. I need to audit a specific feature branch against them.

YOUR OUTPUT — a numbered rubric, in two sections:

SECTION A — CHECKABLE RULES
Every rule that constrains how UI code is written, where each can be mechanically checked against a file. For each:
  - ID (R1, R2, ...)
  - RULE: one sentence, in your own words
  - PREDICATE: a concrete, checkable statement. Something a reviewer could evaluate as true/false against a given file — e.g. "a component's styling lives in a co-located <name>.css.ts registered in theme/components/index.ts, not in JSX props" — NOT a vague aspiration like "styling should be consistent".
  - SOURCE: which of the three docs, and the section heading it came from.

SECTION B — GUIDANCE (NOT CHECKABLE)
Rules that are real but cannot be reduced to a per-file predicate (process, judgement, estimation, team rhythm). Same fields minus PREDICATE. These must NOT be mixed into Section A — a rubric row that cannot be checked will produce a fake audit finding.

SECTION C — INTERNAL DISAGREEMENTS
Anywhere the three documents contradict each other, or where one says something a reader would reasonably interpret two ways. State both readings. Do not resolve them.

FOCUS the rubric on what an audit of a page-and-components feature branch would actually test:
- how a design value resolves (tokens, CSS custom properties, theme scales) and what fails silently
- component structure and the atom/molecule/organism split
- what an override does and does not intercept
- styling surface: recipes vs JSX props vs global classes
- data flow: container vs presentational, hooks, where fetching lives
- microcopy and content sourcing
- testing expectations per layer
- accessibility expectations
- Storybook expectations
- handling absent/unavailable data and design gaps

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- READ-ONLY. Do not write, create or modify any file.
- These documents are LOCAL-ONLY and must never be quoted at length or cited by filename in anything that could reach a git repository. In your report, paraphrase every rule in your own words. Cite source only as "uiBuild §N — <heading>" style short references so I can trace them locally. Never reproduce more than a short phrase verbatim.
- Do not evaluate any code in this pass. You are producing the measuring stick only, not measuring anything.
- If a rule appears in more than one document, state it once and list both sources.

Return the rubric as your final report. Be exhaustive on Section A — a missed rule is a missed audit finding.

16	## 1. How a value resolves
17	
18	### The pipeline is one-way
19	
20	```
21	theme/foundation/*.ts   ← source of truth (Tier 1)
22	        ↓
23	zimmTokens.ts           ← DERIVED. Never hand-edit.
24	        ↓
25	--zimm-* CSS custom properties
26	        ↓
27	recipes: <name>.css.ts / theme/components/*.ts
28	        ↓
29	component JSX
30	```
31	
32	`zimmTokens.ts` imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/
33	`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid` from their owning files rather than
34	retyping values. The only literals left in it are 7 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with
35	no named-scale equivalent.
36	
37	**A Tier 1 comment is wrong about those 7.** `theme/index.ts:47` says the 15 numeric aliases
38	*"are duplicates of the named scale."* `overrideStyling.md:83-85` says 7 of them are not, and
39	`overrideStyling.md` is right: `025` (1px), `700` (28px), `1100` (44px), `1200` (48px),
40	`1300` (52px), `3500` (140px), `4500` (180px) are hardcoded in `zimmTokens.ts`; the other 8
41	derive from `spacing`.
42	
43	### The registration reality — this is the one that breaks layouts
44	
45	`theme/index.ts` registers the Zimmermann scale as **`space` only** (line 56). `sizes`,
46	`fontSizes`, `lineHeights` and `letterSpacings` are deliberately **not** registered, because
47	registering them would restyle the base retail-react-app at ~199 call sites.
48	
49	| Prop family | Reads | Bare key like `'xl'` |
50	|---|---|---|
51	| `margin` `padding` `gap` | `theme.space` ✅ registered | correct |
52	| `width` `height` `boxSize` `min/maxWidth/Height` | `theme.sizes` ❌ not registered | **falls through to Chakra's defaults** |
53	| `fontSize` `lineHeight` `letterSpacing` | ❌ not registered | wrong value, or nothing |
54	
55	Measured blow-up range: **8×–112×**. `width: 'xl'` resolves through `theme.sizes.xl` = 36rem
56	= **576px** — that shipped, blew the footer contact icons to 576px, and destroyed the layout
57	on every page. Worse: `s`, `m`, `l` are **absent** from Chakra's `sizes`, so those
58	declarations are dropped entirely and silently.
59	
60	Typography has the same twin. `fontSize: '2xs'` emits 0.625rem where 0.875rem was intended;
61	`fontSize: '4xs'` emits nothing at all.
62	
63	**Live unfixed instance:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:311` has `fontSize="l"`,
64	which emits nothing. Pre-existing, out of scope for every PR that has touched that file since.
65	`recipeGuards.test.ts` cannot reach it — it walks the registered recipe map only, and this is
66	a JSX prop. Its own `SCOPE:` note says so.
67	
68	**The rule:** on a sizing or typography prop, always the CSS var —
69	`width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`, never `width: 'xl'`. Spacing props are fine with bare keys as
70	far as *correctness* goes; house style is a separate question, below.

72	### [CORRECTED] `var(--zimm-*)` in component JSX is now required, not a smell
73	
74	An earlier revision of this document said component JSX should use `textStyle` plus semantic
75	token strings (`color="text.default"`, `padding="m"`), and that seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` was
76	a signal to look closer. **That is inverted from the current rule and following it now fails
77	review.**
78	
79	`overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 2 and `css.md` both state it plainly:
80	
81	```tsx
82	// ❌ a bare Chakra/theme token string
83	<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />
84	
85	// ✅ the raw var(--zimm-*) reference
86	<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
87	```
88	
89	The stated reason is **house style, not correctness**: a bare key resolves to the identical
90	value on a registered scale, but it forces a reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s
91	registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. A `var()` reference is
92	unambiguous at every call site.
93	
94	`textStyle` is the one legitimate bare key — there is no `var()` for the composite expansion,
95	only for its individual pieces.
96	
97	**And it can never emit one.** `zimmTokens.ts` imports *from* `typography.ts`, so the reverse
98	would be a circular import; `textStyle` therefore always expands to resolved literals at build
99	time. **This is correct behaviour, not a defect** — and it means roughly **85% of what an
100	emitted-CSS audit flags as "raw literals" is `textStyle` working as designed.** Read any
101	`audit:tokens` output with that in mind.
102	
103	**What survives from the old advice, and is still the main point:** brand values mostly should
104	not be in JSX at all. Measured on `develop` 2026-08-25 — `var(--zimm-*)` appears in **14
105	theme files on `develop`** (10 co-located `<name>.css.ts` + 4 under `theme/components/`) — 18 in
106	the current working tree, which adds four uncommitted product-view recipes — and in exactly
107	**one** component `.tsx`: `footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44,62`, a conditional
108	`paddingLeft` that no Chakra prop expresses. So the practice is: type via `textStyle`,
109	colour and spacing into the recipe, `var()` in JSX only for a genuine prop-system gap.
110	
111	**Live violations right now:** `ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductName/index.tsx:20` and
112	`zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:23` both use `color="text.default"`.

114	### Value equality is not token equality
115	
116	Before replacing a literal with a token, three checks — all three must pass:
117	
118	1. **Same unit?** `rem` and `px` are not interchangeable. Swapping `3rem` for a px-defined
119	   alias is a **WCAG 1.4.4 regression**, not a tidy-up.
120	2. **Same semantic scale?** A spacing value and a sizing value that happen to be equal are not
121	   the same token.
122	3. **Is the target permitted?** The numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases are **class-only** —
123	   never in JSX or a recipe.
124	
125	Three real false positives died on these: `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` → `--zimm-scale-1200`
126	(check 1), `SIZE_COL_NAV` (check 2), and `SIZE_MODAL_SUB` ≡ `breakpoints.sm`, which was pure
127	coincidence.
128	
129	### The real invariant is single-sourcing, not `var()` syntax
130	
131	Ask of any value: *is this typed more than once?* Not: *is this a `var()`?* An audit built on
132	syntax generates mostly noise.
133	
134	PR #56 reduced `foundation/`'s hand-typed literals from 237 to 64 — **173 were duplicates**,
135	the same `24px` appearing in `typography.ts` and again in `zimmTokens.ts`. Two later PRs
136	recreated that duplication one layer up without noticing: PR #52 hand-rebuilt in `sx` what
137	`textStyle="heading3"` already gave, five times; PR #55 added `cssVars.ts`, 241 lines mirroring
138	`zimmTokens.ts`'s keys as `var()` strings plus a reimplementation of seven registered text
139	styles. It was removed — a 245-line deletion; at its peak it had 10 consumer files and 148 references.
140	
141	Both misreads passed CodeRabbit. It confirmed every correctness finding and raised **zero**
142	architecture findings.
143	
144	### Units
145	
146	- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with root font-size or browser zoom (WCAG 1.4.4) —
147	  type and spacing. Sub-pixel letter-spacing values keep a trailing `// -0.12px` comment for
148	  traceability, since they don't round to clean rem.
149	- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should *not* scale — border widths, focus-ring offsets.
150	- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts`, deliberate so media queries shift with zoom)
151	  and other genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

155	## 2. Chakra behaviours that fail silently
156	
157	Seven mechanisms. None produces an error, a warning, or a failing type-check.
158	
159	**0. Always declare your own `parts` array.** A recipe with no `parts` inherits the base's
160	list, so any Zimmermann part you add is undeclared and silently unstyled.
161	
162	**1. `extendTheme` deep-merges — it does not replace.** A recipe named `Footer` merges into
163	base SFCC's `Footer` rather than replacing it, inheriting parts you never wrote. Namespace
164	everything: `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`. `recipeGuards.test.ts` enforces this with
165	`INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` — those three are deliberate; anything
166	else must be namespaced.
167	
168	**1b. The merge reorders keys.** A key that already exists in the base keeps the **base's**
169	position in the merged object; a key you add that the base lacks is appended **last**. That is
170	the mechanism behind a shorthand resetting a longhand you wrote first — the order in your file
171	is not the order that ships. Inspect what actually applies:
172	
173	```js
174	theme.components.Header.baseStyle   // merged — what actually applies
175	```
176	
177	**2. A recipe unit test cannot catch the merge.** `extendTheme` does **not** populate
178	`theme.__cssMap` — only `ChakraProvider` does, via `toCSSVar`. So a direct `css()(theme)`
179	assertion in Vitest passes vacuously against an unmerged object.
180	
181	**3. Compound values never tokenise.** Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value.
182	`padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser. Use axis props
183	(`paddingInline`, `paddingBlock`).
184	
185	**4. A shorthand declared after a longhand resets it.** `padding: 0` after `paddingBlock`
186	wipes it. Order matters; prefer the axis props throughout.
187	
188	**5. `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"`** as a style prop, merged *after* `__css`, so a `p:`
189	in your recipe size is discarded. **Size it with `minW`/`minH`** — which is also how you hit the
190	24×24 target-size requirement.
191	
192	**6. Register the recipe or destructuring throws at runtime.** Chakra resolves a recipe by the
193	string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path — so co-location is free, but the
194	key must be in `theme/components/index.ts`.
195	
196	**7. Breakpoint tokens conflict with Chakra's.** `BP.desktop` is 64em; Chakra's `lg` is 62em
197	and `xl` is 80em. A responsive array silently steps at the wrong width. Write explicit media
198	queries:
199	
200	```ts
201	[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
202	```
203	
204	The array shorthand also puts a bare token key at every step, and the guard flags all four.

208	## 3. Component structure
209	
210	### Placement — settled
211	
212	```
213	overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/index.tsx
214	```
215	
216	Being under `components/` is load-bearing for the registry generator, which scans that path.
217	
218	**Three casing families, each correct in its own context. Do not generalise between them:**
219	
220	| Family | Casing | Why |
221	|---|---|---|
222	| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | must match upstream's import path |
223	| ui-kit component | `zimmButton/` camelCase | Zimmermann-authored — the default rule |
224	| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | mirrors upstream exactly |
225	
226	Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Note the theme key is
227	PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`) while its recipe file is camelCase.
228	
229	### Tier is by composition, not visual size
230	
231	Read it off the imports, not the DOM:
232	
233	- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit. `zimmModal` is an atom despite being portal + backdrop +
234	  `role="dialog"` chrome, because it owns no content (`maxWidth`, `labelledBy`, children all
235	  come from the caller).
236	- **molecule** — composes atoms with light local logic. `zimmInputAction` = TextInput + Button
237	  + local validation state.
238	- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**. `zimmSubscribeSection`
239	  owns the subscribe state machine.
240	
241	An icon passed as a prop doesn't count (`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom). Slotted
242	children don't count.
243	
244	**Storybook `title` is a different axis from the folder.** Folder = composition depth;
245	`title` = domain. `zimmModal` (atom) → `Elements/`; `zimmSubscribeSection` (organism) →
246	`Forms/`; `Footer` → `Layout/`. Don't conflate them.
247	
248	### Styling surface — a registered recipe, always
249	
250	Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not a plain stylesheet. The recipe may live beside
251	the component as `<name>.css.ts` or centrally in `theme/components/` — Chakra resolves by
252	string key, so this is purely organisational.
253	
254	The argument against authoring in a stylesheet is worth keeping: a stylesheet can only see
255	`var(--zimm-*)`, which is **derived output at the bottom of the pipeline**. Author there and
256	you lose `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, and the theme
257	drift-guard tests. Not bad CSS — the wrong end of the pipeline.
258	
259	For a bespoke component wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is the bridge:
260	native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`.
261	
262	**Co-location changes who reviews it.** `CODEOWNERS:186`
263	(`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only) is placed **last** among the
264	`components/` rules, and CODEOWNERS is last-match-wins, not most-specific-wins. So a `.css.ts`
265	inside `footer/` drops the Tier 2 approver requirement the surrounding directory carries,
266	while `footer/index.tsx` keeps it. The stated rationale: a co-located recipe *composes
267	established tokens*; authoring a new token still means `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1).
268	
269	`overrideStyling.md` flags its own inconsistency here rather than papering over it —
270	`zimmButton.css.ts` keys the app-wide `Button` recipe and is no longer designer-gated.
271	
272	### No data-fetching in `components/`
273	
274	Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props. Data-fetching belongs in
275	`overrides/app/pages/` or a container.
276	
277	**One documented exception:** Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks (`useIntl`,
278	`useUiCopy`) may be called from any component including presentational leaves, because they
279	read from a Provider mounted above the route tree. Narrow by design — content identical for
280	every consumer regardless of route, not anything that varies per page.
281	
282	**Their no-Provider behaviour differs, and it matters for tests.** `useUiCopy` degrades:
283	`useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`, one line, renders with zero setup. **`useIntl`
284	throws** (`invariantIntlContext`), and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by the base SFCC `_app`,
285	not `_app-config` — a strictly narrower subtree. Any Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer
286	must wrap it.

322	## 4. What an override actually intercepts
323	
324	Three silent failure modes. In each, the override compiles, resolves, and never runs.
325	
326	**1. The resolver is webpack-only.** `ccExtensibility` in `package.json` redirects
327	`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` in the **real app build only**.
328	`.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to `node_modules`, and `vitest.config.ts`
329	doesn't touch it. So a base-path import of an already-overridden component builds correctly in
330	the shipped app and silently renders the **unstyled base version** in Storybook and Vitest —
331	the story looks like it's exercising your override and isn't.
332	
333	When importing a component that already has an override, use a **relative path**
334	(`'../swatch-group'`), not the base path.
335	
336	**2. A relative barrel re-export is not rewritten.** The attractive play — override
337	`shared/ui/<Name>` so branded styling propagates into base cart, checkout and account for free
338	— **does not work.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` does `export {Button} from './Button'`, a
339	relative export the resolver does not rewrite. And the consumption pattern is the wrong way
340	round: **212 base files import the barrel (195 excluding tests); 0 import `shared/ui/Button`.** The override
341	intercepts nothing.
342	
343	**3. A conditional render of an alternate module.** Overriding a component doesn't help if the
344	parent renders something else on that route. `footer` never reaches `/checkout`.
345	
346	**The generalised check**, before scoping any story around "override X and it propagates":
347	
348	```bash
349	grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
350	  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
351	```
352	
353	### The SFCC bridge pattern
354	
355	If a component is used internally by SFCC's own base components, its **default export must
356	stay a faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour.
357	Put Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps it.
358	
359	⚠️ **No worked precedent exists in this repo.** `product-tile` is still base, `CardBaseline`
360	returns zero hits across `overrides/`, and `grep -rn forwardRef overrides/` returns one file.
361	Whoever needs this pattern first will be establishing it, not copying it.
362	
363	Where token-driven theming suffices, a theme recipe is preferable to a second export — the
364	prop-narrowing that motivated `CardBaseline` isn't needed for styling alone.

368	## 5. Figma to code
369	
370	### The discriminator is node type, not a fudge factor
371	
372	- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`,
373	  `text-box-edge: cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts:
374	  "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs 18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
375	- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — a delta here is a
376	  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against 45/68 was a real gap, and a naive
377	  "it's just cap height" rule would have wrongly dismissed it.
378	
379	**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one
380	is a defect. Three contact items all sitting at +7 after every real cause was removed = the
381	heading's cap box.
382	
383	**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.css.ts`, deriving from
384	`lineHeight` + 4.5px padding produced 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.
385	
386	### There are two Figma files and comparisons must be like-for-like
387	
388	`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (design system) and `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states).
389	Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page
390	file produced two wrong conclusions in a row — first "the slot is 59px in both states"
391	(actually `Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap
392	change 40→24: the design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix
393	that suppressed intended growth when the 68px padded box was already correct.
394	
395	### Frames are not breakpoints
396	
397	Frames exist at 402/1023/1440; breakpoint tokens are 768/860/1024. The unframed **768–1022
398	band was genuinely broken** — 18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels — and covers three iPad
399	models in portrait. `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents *breaking*, not *shrinking*: the row refused to
400	break, so the words broke instead.
401	
402	### Type metrics
403	
404	The fallback stack renders roughly **13% wider** than Futura Round, which is why serving the
405	real faces matters for parity review. `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable
406	families and is useless — compare widths instead.
407	
408	### Measurement method
409	
410	**Subtract non-component bands before comparing totals** — the footer compares against 476,
411	not 606, once the `Disclaimer` band is excluded. **Isolate causes by cumulative in-DOM
412	mutation, one candidate at a time.** Measure `y` relative to the component root (Figma reports
413	frame-relative coordinates). Use
414	`domcontentloaded`, never `networkidle`, on a dev server. Dismiss the consent banner first.
415	`Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths to *prove* a wrap point. **Mutation-test layout
416	fixes at mobile** — two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only because a taller sibling column masked
417	them.
418	
419	**A design nudge is still spec.** Ship it and raise the question — don't silently "correct"
420	it, and don't silently ignore it. Document the deviation at the point of use.
421	
422	### No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect
423	
424	`width: 'xl'` resolving to 576px destroyed the footer on every page while passing `tsc`,
425	`eslint`, `vitest`, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and the Storybook a11y run. Only rendering
426	beside Figma found it.

430	## 6. Layout mechanics
431	
432	Six mechanisms, each with the fix that actually worked.
433	
434	1. **A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line.** `width: min-content`
435	   resolves to the widest unbreakable run — usually what you want when a column should hug its
436	   longest word rather than its container.
437	
438	2. **`minHeight` plus `align-items: center` loses leading when content wraps.** The centring
439	   discards the extra line's leading rather than growing the box. Derive height from
440	   `lineHeight` plus padding instead of reserving a `minHeight`.
441	
442	3. **An inline child inside a block parent leaks descender space.** A block-level `<li>`
443	   wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` gets a line box whose strut sits below the baseline —
444	   measured **25.5px against the anchor's own 24px**, leaking 1.5px per row (3px on a wrapped
445	   label) and making the footer's links column 9px taller than Figma's 158px.
446	   **Fix: `display: flex` on the `<li>`**, which removes the line box entirely.
447	   `footerNavColumn.css.ts:69` is the shipped instance.
448	   ⚠️ `display: block` is the **bug**, not the fix.
449	
450	4. **Give the gap to the heading, not the column.** If the design nests a group inside a stack
451	   with no gap, don't reproduce it as a sibling in a gapped flex container — the container's
452	   gap then applies where the design has none. Put the spacing on the heading's `marginBottom`.
453	
454	5. **`flexWrap: nowrap` prevents breaking, not shrinking.** The row refuses to break, so the
455	   words break instead. This is what broke the unframed 768–1022 band.
456	
457	6. **A non-breaking space must be the `\u00A0` escape**, not a literal character in source —
458	   invisible to review and unpredictable under reformatting. Note the dependency it creates:
459	   production copy has to carry the same character.
460	
461	**A solution window measured in single pixels is a coincidence, not a tolerance.** The footer's
462	viable column cap was **[131, 132.9) — 1.9px wide**. Treat that as a signal the constraint set
463	is over-determined, not as a fix that happens to work.

465	## 7. Building against absent data
466	
467	### Three patterns, only the first correct
468	
469	**Guard, then render inert but perceivable.** Never render nothing where a control was
470	promised; never render a control that can't act.
471	
472	- **An empty-string fallback is a layout bug** — `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that
473	  **keeps its margins**, measured as a roughly 64px void. It doesn't collapse; it reserves
474	  space for nothing.
475	- **A silent element swap actively lies** — it promises an affordance that isn't there.
476	- **Fix at the atom**, not at each call site.
477	
478	### The three-tier policy — the most reusable decision in the footer build
479	
480	Behaviour differs by what the content *is*:
481	
482	| Content class | Behaviour | Why |
483	|---|---|---|
484	| **Structural** (`footerConfig`) | render **nothing** — `if (!footerData) return null` | no fallback to placeholder once wired to live data, so an outage doesn't ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers |
485	| **Microcopy** (`uiCopy`) | fall back to the **English literal** | losing a button label to an outage should never blank a control |
486	| **Per-item destination** (a contact href) | degrade **that item only** to a labelled non-interactive `<span>` | perceivable, but no false affordance |
487	
488	The per-item case is the carefully argued one: no `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing promises an
489	action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4) — but **labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so
490	a screen-reader user learns the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoiding the 1.1.1
491	information loss an earlier `aria-hidden` caused).
492	
493	The same treatment is reused three times for "control with no action": the contact fallback,
494	`ZimmNavItem`'s no-href branch (renders a `<button>` that doesn't navigate), and `BottomBar`'s
495	locale placeholder (a `<div>`, deliberately not a `<button>`).
496	
497	### Never branch on localised CMS text
498	
499	`footerNavGroup` carries `showContactChannels: boolean` rather than matching
500	`heading === 'Contact'` — because `heading` is localised and silently stops matching the moment
501	an editor writes "Kontakt" or "Contacto". This footer ships to eight storefronts.
502	
503	### Guarding hrefs
504	
505	Every CMS-sourced href passes `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor. The subtlety: WHATWG URL
506	parsing strips C0 control characters, tab, LF and CR *before* scheme detection, so a naive
507	`^javascript:` regex is bypassed by `java\tscript:`. **Normalise, then test.**
508	
509	---
510	
511	## 8. CMS data and the tier reality
512	
513	New section. The footer rendered correctly in dev and was blank on the test tier, and nothing
514	in the component was wrong.
515	
516	### Content types and entries promote by different mechanisms
517	
518	| | Content **types** (schema) | Content (**entries**) |
519	|---|---|---|
520	| Mechanism | org-scoped Environment Template | *nothing automated* |
521	| Build | `npm run sync:contentful` | — |
522	| Deploy | `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` | — |
523	
524	**A template cannot carry entries — this is structural.** The SDK type has exactly two slots:
525	
526	```ts
527	// contentful-management/dist/types/entities/environment-template.d.ts:31-34
528	entities: {
529	    contentTypeTemplates: Array<ContentTypeTemplateProps>;
530	    editorInterfaceTemplates: Array<EditorInterfaceTemplateProps>;
531	};
532	```
533	
534	No `entries`, no `assets`. The only entry-writing code in the repo is `seedRegions.mjs:71-72`,
535	which handles the 11 `region` entries and nothing else.
536	
537	### Verified tier state, 2026-08-25
538	
539	| tier | content types | published entries |
540	|---|---|---|
541	| **dev** | **14** | **42** (+3 assets) |
542	| test / sit / uat / staging | **0** | **0** |
543	| prod | no environment id configured | — |
544	
545	The environments exist — the CDA returned `total: 0`, not `NotFound`. Nothing has ever been
546	promoted out of dev.
547	
548	**The template covers 5 of dev's 14 types** — `footerConfig`, `footerNavGroup`, `link`,
549	`region`, `uiCopy`. The other 9 exist only inside the dev environment, UI-authored, with no
550	code representation, and `install:contentful` cannot move them.
551	
552	**There is no forward content promotion in this repo at all.** The actual release model is the
553	alias flip in `promoteAlias.mjs`: clone master → install template → author and verify →
554	repoint `production`/`master`. Content moves *backwards* (master → clone), never forwards.
555	
556	### Fetch-depth is load-bearing
557	
558	`include: 3` is not arbitrary. At depth 2 the `regions` array arrives as unresolved stubs,
559	`region.fields.siteId` throws, the `.catch` swallows it, and the **entire footer renders
560	nothing**. A resolution-depth mistake looks identical to a network failure from the page.
561	
562	### Locale is not passed on any Contentful fetch
563	
564	`useContentful.ts:110` builds a URL with `content_type`, `access_token` and `include` only, so
565	the footer and `uiCopy` get the space default on all eight storefronts. Three invocation sites
566	across two production files. (`pages/experience/` and `pages/contentfulPreview/` *do* pass
567	`localeCode` — the gap is the shared hook, not every caller.) Blocked on a shared-
568	hook signature change, which is a team RFC.
569	
570	### The check to run before promising a component works on a tier
571	
572	```bash
573	curl -s "https://cdn.contentful.com/spaces/<space>/environments/<env>/entries?content_type=<type>&limit=1" \
574	  -H "Authorization: Bearer <that tier's delivery token>"
575	```
576	
577	`total: 1` means it will render. `unknownContentType` means the model was never installed.
578	Note the CDA returns an unreliable `total` at `limit=0` — use `limit=1`.
579	
580	---
581	
582	## 9. Accessibility patterns
583	
584	Six recurring success criteria and what each actually demanded.
585	
586	- **1.1.1** — a degraded control must stay *labelled*, not `aria-hidden`. Silence is
587	  information loss.
588	- **1.4.4 / 1.4.10** — `rem` for anything that must survive zoom; a modal panel needs
589	  `maxHeight` + `overflowY` or tall content centres half-off-screen and is unreachable.
590	- **2.4.4 / 3.2.4** — no `href` and no `tabIndex` on a control that cannot act, so nothing
591	  promises an action that can't be performed.
592	- **2.5.8** — 24×24 minimum target size, which is a WCAG **2.2** addition and easy to miss if
593	  working from a 2.1 checklist.
594	- **2.5.3 Label in name** — the accessible name must *contain* the visible label.
595	- **3.2.5** — a link leaving the site gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and a suffix in its
596	  accessible name. That is the project's external-link standard; it lives nowhere else.
597	- **Focus** — a programmatic `.focus()` does **not** match `:focus-visible`. A focus ring
598	  styled only on `:focus-visible` will not appear after a scripted focus move.
599	- **Portal + focus trap** — when `activeElement` is outside the trap, the trap must handle it
600	  rather than assume containment.
601	
602	Every `IconButton` needs `aria-label`; every `<img>` needs `alt` (`alt=""` for decorative).
603	Note the ast-grep rule matches `^img$` only, so Chakra's `<Image>` is invisible to it, and its
604	`aria-label` check does not match `aria-labelledby`.
605	
606	---
607	
608	## 10. Verification: what actually proves anything
609	
610	### The integrity principle
611	
612	> The verification instrument was built from the same belief as the thing it verified, and was
613	> never made to fail on purpose.
614	
615	That is the single recurring failure mode. A green check that was never proven capable of going
616	red carries no information.
617	
618	Catalogued instances, all self-caught after reporting a false all-clear: a `safeHref` suite
619	reported "well covered, 3 layers" whose 13 cases contained **zero backslashes** — the exact
620	vector already named; a `fontFace` test iterating an empty array; a mutation test that
621	"passed" because `perl -pi` works line-at-a-time and cannot match `\n`; a recipe parity check
622	that false-alarmed three times on recipes whose `baseStyle` is a **function**; a literal-count
623	sweep that inflated 19→41 by matching `.rem` inside `removeEventListener`.
624	
625	### Copy the non-vacuity meta-test
626	
627	`recipeGuards.test.ts` includes `test('collect() actually walks the registered recipes')`
628	precisely because every other guard asserts `toEqual([])`, which an empty input satisfies.
629	Stubbing `components` to `{}` turned the whole file green — verified.
630	
631	Same shape for layout assertions: a pure before/after equality is satisfied vacuously by a
632	collapsed container (`display:none`, `height:0`, an ancestor `display:none` — and every rect
633	is 0 in jsdom). **Anchor the measurement above zero first.**
634	
635	And resolve a function-form `baseStyle` across **all** boolean prop combinations, not the
636	default one. The original bug hid down a conditional branch a single-resolution walk never
637	entered.
638	
639	### Green tests that encode the bug
640	
641	A suite can test *around* a defect. The region tie-break suite had a case named "order of the
642	tied candidates does not change the outcome" that used only **distinct** timestamps — the one
643	arrangement already order-independent. It passed while the bug was live.
644	
645	Mutation testing is necessary but not sufficient: it proves the check *can* fail, not that it
646	fails for the right reason.
647	
648	### [CORRECTED] What is and is not gated
649	
650	**a11y IS gated.** An earlier belief — repeated four times in one session and again by a fresh
651	analysis this week — was that a11y is ungated because there is no `.storybook/test-runner.js`.
652	**That is Storybook 8 knowledge and is wrong for what is installed.**
653	`@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4`'s `dist/setup-page-script.js:390-397` reads
654	`story.parameters?.a11y?.test` and throws when it `=== "error"`; `.storybook/preview.tsx:44`
655	sets exactly that. No `test-runner.js` is needed. **Do not delete that `preview.tsx` block.**
656	
657	Honest rider: the gate has never been made to fail on purpose, so by the standard above it is
658	**unproven, not absent**.
659	
660	**Gated nowhere at all:** `eslint`, `prettier`, `tsc --noEmit`, `audit:tokens`, any CSS bundle
661	budget, test coverage. `npm run lint` currently fails repo-wide on pre-existing prettier errors
662	and CI never notices.
663	
664	**A skipped required check counts as passing.** Live on PR #59: all four suites reported
665	`skipping` — including both *required* checks — while `mergeable: true`. `detect-changes` uses
666	`since_last_remote_commit`, and a final push touching only registry files fell outside every
667	allow-list. A 93-commit PR became merge-eligible with **zero test evidence on its head SHA**.
668	Read `gh pr checks` for `skipping`, not just for green.
669	
670	**A named gate that cannot fail:** `npm run test:contracts` is `echo 'TODO…' && exit 0`, and
671	it is a hard `needs` of `sit-gate`.
672	
673	### Harness traps
674	
675	- **`test-storybook` needs a *built* Storybook.** Dev-server runs made four mutation results
676	  uninterpretable.
677	- **Vitest does not run `play`.**
678	- **jsdom always provides `window`**, so an SSR branch needs `// @vitest-environment node`.
679	- **Every jsdom rect is 0** — layout assertions there are meaningless.
680	- **`ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest.** It imports the base SFCC icons barrel, whose top-level
681	  `AmexSymbol.viewBox = ...` fails because SVG imports resolve to raw path strings here.
682	  Unfixable from a test file (`vitest.config.ts` is Tier 1). Mock at the smallest surface:
683	  ```ts
684	  vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))
685	  ```
686	  …or forward `aria-label`/`aria-hidden` when an assertion depends on the accessible name.
687	- **Portalled content is scoped to `document.body`, not `canvasElement`.** `canvasElement` is
688	  `#storybook-root`, a *sibling* of the portal target. Measured: `canvasElement.innerHTML` is
689	  41 characters, 0 dialogs inside the canvas against 1 in the document. A canvas-scoped
690	  `getByRole` fails immediately; `findByRole` fails after ~1002ms; the body-scoped form passes
691	  in 1–2ms. `testing.md:128`'s "never reach into `document`" has no portal carve-out — that is
692	  a documentation defect, not a code one.
693	- **`@storybook/test` is not installed.** `testing.md:115` prescribes it; Storybook 10 moved it
694	  to `storybook/test`. Following that line verbatim breaks.
695	
696	### The gap no tool covers
697	
698	Duplication and reuse. No tool detects "this is a second Button." Nothing catches a bare token
699	key used as a JSX prop. Nothing catches a layout defect. Nothing catches a component whose data
700	doesn't exist on the tier it ships to.
701	
702	---
703	
704	## 11. Signposts in the repo that point at nothing
705	
706	Each of these has already cost time.
707	
708	- **`overrides.md` does not exist.** `overrideStyling.md:4,112,179` references it three times
709	  and positions it as the companion doc defining module-replacement correctness. It exists only
710	  on two unmerged spike branches.
711	- **`overrideStyling.md` is orphaned and unsynced.** `AGENTS.md` never references it
712	  (`grep -c` → 0). `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs`'s manifest omits it, along with `css.md`,
713	  `components.md`, `typescript.md` and `tagging.md` — three of which are in `conventions.md`'s
714	  own "See also" list. The largest rules file, holding the entire styling hierarchy, is
715	  invisible to Cursor and Copilot.
716	- **The rules set is split on its own component convention.** `components.md` and
717	  `conventions.md` contain **zero** occurrences of `ui-kits`, `atoms`, `molecules` or
718	  `organisms`. `new-component/SKILL.md:29` still scaffolds to the flat path.
719	  `.docs/architecture.md` contradicts itself — `:136` cites the correct
720	  `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts` while `:130`/`:139` prescribe a
721	  `components/custom/` directory that has never existed.
722	- **[CORRECTED] `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` now exists.** Earlier notes said it didn't. It
723	  was built 2026-08-23 and `npm run audit:tokens` is wired. It is still **not in CI** — a

731	  never has. The job runs on every dev deploy and is a guarded permanent no-op — no sprint tag
732	  has ever been created.

# UI Build — Knowledge & Context

Technical reference only — no roles, no process, no review workflow. Those live in
`fedLead-playbook.md` (the role) and `fedBuild-manual.md` (the procedure).

Every claim here was measured against the installed toolchain, not inherited from an
earlier note. Beliefs that turned out to be wrong are marked **[CORRECTED]** and the
correction is kept visible rather than silently overwritten — a claim that was confidently
wrong once is worth flagging so it isn't re-derived.

*Re-verified 2026-08-25 against `develop` @ `8362b3c` (PR #59 merged) with
`feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info` checked out.*

---

## 1. How a value resolves

### The pipeline is one-way

```
theme/foundation/*.ts   ← source of truth (Tier 1)
        ↓
zimmTokens.ts           ← DERIVED. Never hand-edit.
        ↓
--zimm-* CSS custom properties
        ↓
recipes: <name>.css.ts / theme/components/*.ts
        ↓
component JSX
```

`zimmTokens.ts` imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/
`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid` from their owning files rather than
retyping values. The only literals left in it are 7 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with
no named-scale equivalent.

**A Tier 1 comment is wrong about those 7.** `theme/index.ts:47` says the 15 numeric aliases
*"are duplicates of the named scale."* `overrideStyling.md:83-85` says 7 of them are not, and
`overrideStyling.md` is right: `025` (1px), `700` (28px), `1100` (44px), `1200` (48px),
`1300` (52px), `3500` (140px), `4500` (180px) are hardcoded in `zimmTokens.ts`; the other 8
derive from `spacing`.

### The registration reality — this is the one that breaks layouts

`theme/index.ts` registers the Zimmermann scale as **`space` only** (line 56). `sizes`,
`fontSizes`, `lineHeights` and `letterSpacings` are deliberately **not** registered, because
registering them would restyle the base retail-react-app at ~199 call sites.

| Prop family | Reads | Bare key like `'xl'` |
|---|---|---|
| `margin` `padding` `gap` | `theme.space` ✅ registered | correct |
| `width` `height` `boxSize` `min/maxWidth/Height` | `theme.sizes` ❌ not registered | **falls through to Chakra's defaults** |
| `fontSize` `lineHeight` `letterSpacing` | ❌ not registered | wrong value, or nothing |

Measured blow-up range: **8×–112×**. `width: 'xl'` resolves through `theme.sizes.xl` = 36rem
= **576px** — that shipped, blew the footer contact icons to 576px, and destroyed the layout
on every page. Worse: `s`, `m`, `l` are **absent** from Chakra's `sizes`, so those
declarations are dropped entirely and silently.

Typography has the same twin. `fontSize: '2xs'` emits 0.625rem where 0.875rem was intended;
`fontSize: '4xs'` emits nothing at all.

**Live unfixed instance:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:311` has `fontSize="l"`,
which emits nothing. Pre-existing, out of scope for every PR that has touched that file since.
`recipeGuards.test.ts` cannot reach it — it walks the registered recipe map only, and this is
a JSX prop. Its own `SCOPE:` note says so.

**The rule:** on a sizing or typography prop, always the CSS var —
`width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`, never `width: 'xl'`. Spacing props are fine with bare keys as
far as *correctness* goes; house style is a separate question, below.

### [CORRECTED] `var(--zimm-*)` in component JSX is now required, not a smell

An earlier revision of this document said component JSX should use `textStyle` plus semantic
token strings (`color="text.default"`, `padding="m"`), and that seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` was
a signal to look closer. **That is inverted from the current rule and following it now fails
review.**

`overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 2 and `css.md` both state it plainly:

```tsx
// ❌ a bare Chakra/theme token string
<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ the raw var(--zimm-*) reference
<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
```

The stated reason is **house style, not correctness**: a bare key resolves to the identical
value on a registered scale, but it forces a reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s
registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. A `var()` reference is
unambiguous at every call site.

`textStyle` is the one legitimate bare key — there is no `var()` for the composite expansion,
only for its individual pieces.

**And it can never emit one.** `zimmTokens.ts` imports *from* `typography.ts`, so the reverse
would be a circular import; `textStyle` therefore always expands to resolved literals at build
time. **This is correct behaviour, not a defect** — and it means roughly **85% of what an
emitted-CSS audit flags as "raw literals" is `textStyle` working as designed.** Read any
`audit:tokens` output with that in mind.

**What survives from the old advice, and is still the main point:** brand values mostly should
not be in JSX at all. Measured on `develop` 2026-08-25 — `var(--zimm-*)` appears in **14
theme files on `develop`** (10 co-located `<name>.css.ts` + 4 under `theme/components/`) — 18 in
the current working tree, which adds four uncommitted product-view recipes — and in exactly
**one** component `.tsx`: `footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44,62`, a conditional
`paddingLeft` that no Chakra prop expresses. So the practice is: type via `textStyle`,
colour and spacing into the recipe, `var()` in JSX only for a genuine prop-system gap.

**Live violations right now:** `ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductName/index.tsx:20` and
`zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:23` both use `color="text.default"`.

### Value equality is not token equality

Before replacing a literal with a token, three checks — all three must pass:

1. **Same unit?** `rem` and `px` are not interchangeable. Swapping `3rem` for a px-defined
   alias is a **WCAG 1.4.4 regression**, not a tidy-up.
2. **Same semantic scale?** A spacing value and a sizing value that happen to be equal are not
   the same token.
3. **Is the target permitted?** The numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases are **class-only** —
   never in JSX or a recipe.

Three real false positives died on these: `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` → `--zimm-scale-1200`
(check 1), `SIZE_COL_NAV` (check 2), and `SIZE_MODAL_SUB` ≡ `breakpoints.sm`, which was pure
coincidence.

### The real invariant is single-sourcing, not `var()` syntax

Ask of any value: *is this typed more than once?* Not: *is this a `var()`?* An audit built on
syntax generates mostly noise.

PR #56 reduced `foundation/`'s hand-typed literals from 237 to 64 — **173 were duplicates**,
the same `24px` appearing in `typography.ts` and again in `zimmTokens.ts`. Two later PRs
recreated that duplication one layer up without noticing: PR #52 hand-rebuilt in `sx` what
`textStyle="heading3"` already gave, five times; PR #55 added `cssVars.ts`, 241 lines mirroring
`zimmTokens.ts`'s keys as `var()` strings plus a reimplementation of seven registered text
styles. It was removed — a 245-line deletion; at its peak it had 10 consumer files and 148 references.

Both misreads passed CodeRabbit. It confirmed every correctness finding and raised **zero**
architecture findings.

### Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with root font-size or browser zoom (WCAG 1.4.4) —
  type and spacing. Sub-pixel letter-spacing values keep a trailing `// -0.12px` comment for
  traceability, since they don't round to clean rem.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should *not* scale — border widths, focus-ring offsets.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts`, deliberate so media queries shift with zoom)
  and other genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

---

## 2. Chakra behaviours that fail silently

Seven mechanisms. None produces an error, a warning, or a failing type-check.

**0. Always declare your own `parts` array.** A recipe with no `parts` inherits the base's
list, so any Zimmermann part you add is undeclared and silently unstyled.

**1. `extendTheme` deep-merges — it does not replace.** A recipe named `Footer` merges into
base SFCC's `Footer` rather than replacing it, inheriting parts you never wrote. Namespace
everything: `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`. `recipeGuards.test.ts` enforces this with
`INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` — those three are deliberate; anything
else must be namespaced.

**1b. The merge reorders keys.** A key that already exists in the base keeps the **base's**
position in the merged object; a key you add that the base lacks is appended **last**. That is
the mechanism behind a shorthand resetting a longhand you wrote first — the order in your file
is not the order that ships. Inspect what actually applies:

```js
theme.components.Header.baseStyle   // merged — what actually applies
```

**2. A recipe unit test cannot catch the merge.** `extendTheme` does **not** populate
`theme.__cssMap` — only `ChakraProvider` does, via `toCSSVar`. So a direct `css()(theme)`
assertion in Vitest passes vacuously against an unmerged object.

**3. Compound values never tokenise.** Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value.
`padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser. Use axis props
(`paddingInline`, `paddingBlock`).

**4. A shorthand declared after a longhand resets it.** `padding: 0` after `paddingBlock`
wipes it. Order matters; prefer the axis props throughout.

**5. `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"`** as a style prop, merged *after* `__css`, so a `p:`
in your recipe size is discarded. **Size it with `minW`/`minH`** — which is also how you hit the
24×24 target-size requirement.

**6. Register the recipe or destructuring throws at runtime.** Chakra resolves a recipe by the
string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path — so co-location is free, but the
key must be in `theme/components/index.ts`.

**7. Breakpoint tokens conflict with Chakra's.** `BP.desktop` is 64em; Chakra's `lg` is 62em
and `xl` is 80em. A responsive array silently steps at the wrong width. Write explicit media
queries:

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
```

The array shorthand also puts a bare token key at every step, and the guard flags all four.

## 3. Component structure

### Placement — settled

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/index.tsx
```

Being under `components/` is load-bearing for the registry generator, which scans that path.

**Three casing families, each correct in its own context. Do not generalise between them:**

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | must match upstream's import path |
| ui-kit component | `zimmButton/` camelCase | Zimmermann-authored — the default rule |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | mirrors upstream exactly |

Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Note the theme key is
PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`) while its recipe file is camelCase.

### Tier is by composition, not visual size

Read it off the imports, not the DOM:

- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit. `zimmModal` is an atom despite being portal + backdrop +
  `role="dialog"` chrome, because it owns no content (`maxWidth`, `labelledBy`, children all
  come from the caller).
- **molecule** — composes atoms with light local logic. `zimmInputAction` = TextInput + Button
  + local validation state.
- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**. `zimmSubscribeSection`
  owns the subscribe state machine.

An icon passed as a prop doesn't count (`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom). Slotted
children don't count.

**Storybook `title` is a different axis from the folder.** Folder = composition depth;
`title` = domain. `zimmModal` (atom) → `Elements/`; `zimmSubscribeSection` (organism) →
`Forms/`; `Footer` → `Layout/`. Don't conflate them.

### Styling surface — a registered recipe, always

Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not a plain stylesheet. The recipe may live beside
the component as `<name>.css.ts` or centrally in `theme/components/` — Chakra resolves by
string key, so this is purely organisational.

The argument against authoring in a stylesheet is worth keeping: a stylesheet can only see
`var(--zimm-*)`, which is **derived output at the bottom of the pipeline**. Author there and
you lose `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, and the theme
drift-guard tests. Not bad CSS — the wrong end of the pipeline.

For a bespoke component wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is the bridge:
native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`.

**Co-location changes who reviews it.** `CODEOWNERS:186`
(`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only) is placed **last** among the
`components/` rules, and CODEOWNERS is last-match-wins, not most-specific-wins. So a `.css.ts`
inside `footer/` drops the Tier 2 approver requirement the surrounding directory carries,
while `footer/index.tsx` keeps it. The stated rationale: a co-located recipe *composes
established tokens*; authoring a new token still means `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1).

`overrideStyling.md` flags its own inconsistency here rather than papering over it —
`zimmButton.css.ts` keys the app-wide `Button` recipe and is no longer designer-gated.

Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props. Data-fetching belongs in
`overrides/app/pages/` or a container.

**One documented exception:** Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks (`useIntl`,
`useUiCopy`) may be called from any component including presentational leaves, because they
read from a Provider mounted above the route tree. Narrow by design — content identical for

## 4. What an override actually intercepts

Three silent failure modes. In each, the override compiles, resolves, and never runs.

**1. The resolver is webpack-only.** `ccExtensibility` in `package.json` redirects
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` in the **real app build only**.
`.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to `node_modules`, and `vitest.config.ts`
doesn't touch it. So a base-path import of an already-overridden component builds correctly in
the shipped app and silently renders the **unstyled base version** in Storybook and Vitest —
the story looks like it's exercising your override and isn't.

When importing a component that already has an override, use a **relative path**
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the base path.

**2. A relative barrel re-export is not rewritten.** The attractive play — override
`shared/ui/<Name>` so branded styling propagates into base cart, checkout and account for free
— **does not work.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` does `export {Button} from './Button'`, a
relative export the resolver does not rewrite. And the consumption pattern is the wrong way
round: **212 base files import the barrel (195 excluding tests); 0 import `shared/ui/Button`.** The override
intercepts nothing.

**3. A conditional render of an alternate module.** Overriding a component doesn't help if the
parent renders something else on that route. `footer` never reaches `/checkout`.

**The generalised check**, before scoping any story around "override X and it propagates":

```bash
grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

### The SFCC bridge pattern

If a component is used internally by SFCC's own base components, its **default export must
stay a faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour.
Put Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps it.

⚠️ **No worked precedent exists in this repo.** `product-tile` is still base, `CardBaseline`
returns zero hits across `overrides/`, and `grep -rn forwardRef overrides/` returns one file.
Whoever needs this pattern first will be establishing it, not copying it.

Where token-driven theming suffices, a theme recipe is preferable to a second export — the
prop-narrowing that motivated `CardBaseline` isn't needed for styling alone.

## 5. Figma to code

### The discriminator is node type, not a fudge factor

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`,
  `text-box-edge: cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts:
  "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs 18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — a delta here is a
  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against 45/68 was a real gap, and a naive
  "it's just cap height" rule would have wrongly dismissed it.

**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one
is a defect. Three contact items all sitting at +7 after every real cause was removed = the
heading's cap box.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.css.ts`, deriving from
`lineHeight` + 4.5px padding produced 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

### There are two Figma files and comparisons must be like-for-like

`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (design system) and `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states).
Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page
file produced two wrong conclusions in a row — first "the slot is 59px in both states"
(actually `Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap
change 40→24: the design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix
that suppressed intended growth when the 68px padded box was already correct.

### Frames are not breakpoints

Frames exist at 402/1023/1440; breakpoint tokens are 768/860/1024. The unframed **768–1022
band was genuinely broken** — 18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels — and covers three iPad
models in portrait. `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents *breaking*, not *shrinking*: the row refused to
break, so the words broke instead.

### Type metrics

The fallback stack renders roughly **13% wider** than Futura Round, which is why serving the
real faces matters for parity review. `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable
families and is useless — compare widths instead.

### Measurement method

**Subtract non-component bands before comparing totals** — the footer compares against 476,
not 606, once the `Disclaimer` band is excluded. **Isolate causes by cumulative in-DOM
mutation, one candidate at a time.** Measure `y` relative to the component root (Figma reports
frame-relative coordinates). Use
`domcontentloaded`, never `networkidle`, on a dev server. Dismiss the consent banner first.
`Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths to *prove* a wrap point. **Mutation-test layout
fixes at mobile** — two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only because a taller sibling column masked
them.

**A design nudge is still spec.** Ship it and raise the question — don't silently "correct"
it, and don't silently ignore it. Document the deviation at the point of use.

### No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect

`width: 'xl'` resolving to 576px destroyed the footer on every page while passing `tsc`,
`eslint`, `vitest`, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and the Storybook a11y run. Only rendering
beside Figma found it.

## 6. Layout mechanics

Six mechanisms, each with the fix that actually worked.

1. **A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line.** `width: min-content`
   resolves to the widest unbreakable run — usually what you want when a column should hug its
   longest word rather than its container.

2. **`minHeight` plus `align-items: center` loses leading when content wraps.** The centring
   discards the extra line's leading rather than growing the box. Derive height from
   `lineHeight` plus padding instead of reserving a `minHeight`.

3. **An inline child inside a block parent leaks descender space.** A block-level `<li>`
   wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` gets a line box whose strut sits below the baseline —
   measured **25.5px against the anchor's own 24px**, leaking 1.5px per row (3px on a wrapped
   label) and making the footer's links column 9px taller than Figma's 158px.
   **Fix: `display: flex` on the `<li>`**, which removes the line box entirely.
   `footerNavColumn.css.ts:69` is the shipped instance.
   ⚠️ `display: block` is the **bug**, not the fix.

4. **Give the gap to the heading, not the column.** If the design nests a group inside a stack
   with no gap, don't reproduce it as a sibling in a gapped flex container — the container's
   gap then applies where the design has none. Put the spacing on the heading's `marginBottom`.

5. **`flexWrap: nowrap` prevents breaking, not shrinking.** The row refuses to break, so the
   words break instead. This is what broke the unframed 768–1022 band.

6. **A non-breaking space must be the `\u00A0` escape**, not a literal character in source —
   invisible to review and unpredictable under reformatting. Note the dependency it creates:
   production copy has to carry the same character.

**A solution window measured in single pixels is a coincidence, not a tolerance.** The footer's
viable column cap was **[131, 132.9) — 1.9px wide**. Treat that as a signal the constraint set
is over-determined, not as a fix that happens to work.

## 7. Building against absent data

### Three patterns, only the first correct

**Guard, then render inert but perceivable.** Never render nothing where a control was
promised; never render a control that can't act.

- **An empty-string fallback is a layout bug** — `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that
  **keeps its margins**, measured as a roughly 64px void. It doesn't collapse; it reserves
  space for nothing.
- **A silent element swap actively lies** — it promises an affordance that isn't there.
- **Fix at the atom**, not at each call site.

### The three-tier policy — the most reusable decision in the footer build

Behaviour differs by what the content *is*:

| Content class | Behaviour | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Structural** (`footerConfig`) | render **nothing** — `if (!footerData) return null` | no fallback to placeholder once wired to live data, so an outage doesn't ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers |
| **Microcopy** (`uiCopy`) | fall back to the **English literal** | losing a button label to an outage should never blank a control |
| **Per-item destination** (a contact href) | degrade **that item only** to a labelled non-interactive `<span>` | perceivable, but no false affordance |

The per-item case is the carefully argued one: no `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing promises an
action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4) — but **labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so
a screen-reader user learns the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoiding the 1.1.1
information loss an earlier `aria-hidden` caused).

The same treatment is reused three times for "control with no action": the contact fallback,
`ZimmNavItem`'s no-href branch (renders a `<button>` that doesn't navigate), and `BottomBar`'s
locale placeholder (a `<div>`, deliberately not a `<button>`).

### Never branch on localised CMS text

`footerNavGroup` carries `showContactChannels: boolean` rather than matching
`heading === 'Contact'` — because `heading` is localised and silently stops matching the moment
an editor writes "Kontakt" or "Contacto". This footer ships to eight storefronts.

### Guarding hrefs

Every CMS-sourced href passes `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor. The subtlety: WHATWG URL
parsing strips C0 control characters, tab, LF and CR *before* scheme detection, so a naive
`^javascript:` regex is bypassed by `java\tscript:`. **Normalise, then test.**

## 9. Accessibility patterns

Six recurring success criteria and what each actually demanded.

- **1.1.1** — a degraded control must stay *labelled*, not `aria-hidden`. Silence is
  information loss.
- **1.4.4 / 1.4.10** — `rem` for anything that must survive zoom; a modal panel needs
  `maxHeight` + `overflowY` or tall content centres half-off-screen and is unreachable.
- **2.4.4 / 3.2.4** — no `href` and no `tabIndex` on a control that cannot act, so nothing
  promises an action that can't be performed.
- **2.5.8** — 24×24 minimum target size, which is a WCAG **2.2** addition and easy to miss if
  working from a 2.1 checklist.
- **2.5.3 Label in name** — the accessible name must *contain* the visible label.
- **3.2.5** — a link leaving the site gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and a suffix in its
  accessible name. That is the project's external-link standard; it lives nowhere else.
- **Focus** — a programmatic `.focus()` does **not** match `:focus-visible`. A focus ring
  styled only on `:focus-visible` will not appear after a scripted focus move.
- **Portal + focus trap** — when `activeElement` is outside the trap, the trap must handle it
  rather than assume containment.

Every `IconButton` needs `aria-label`; every `<img>` needs `alt` (`alt=""` for decorative).
Note the ast-grep rule matches `^img$` only, so Chakra's `<Image>` is invisible to it, and its
`aria-label` check does not match `aria-labelledby`.

## 10. Verification: what actually proves anything

### The integrity principle

> The verification instrument was built from the same belief as the thing it verified, and was
> never made to fail on purpose.

That is the single recurring failure mode. A green check that was never proven capable of going
red carries no information.

Catalogued instances, all self-caught after reporting a false all-clear: a `safeHref` suite
reported "well covered, 3 layers" whose 13 cases contained **zero backslashes** — the exact
vector already named; a `fontFace` test iterating an empty array; a mutation test that
"passed" because `perl -pi` works line-at-a-time and cannot match `\n`; a recipe parity check
that false-alarmed three times on recipes whose `baseStyle` is a **function**; a literal-count
sweep that inflated 19→41 by matching `.rem` inside `removeEventListener`.

### Copy the non-vacuity meta-test

`recipeGuards.test.ts` includes `test('collect() actually walks the registered recipes')`
precisely because every other guard asserts `toEqual([])`, which an empty input satisfies.
Stubbing `components` to `{}` turned the whole file green — verified.

Same shape for layout assertions: a pure before/after equality is satisfied vacuously by a
collapsed container (`display:none`, `height:0`, an ancestor `display:none` — and every rect
is 0 in jsdom). **Anchor the measurement above zero first.**

And resolve a function-form `baseStyle` across **all** boolean prop combinations, not the
default one. The original bug hid down a conditional branch a single-resolution walk never
entered.

### Green tests that encode the bug

A suite can test *around* a defect. The region tie-break suite had a case named "order of the
tied candidates does not change the outcome" that used only **distinct** timestamps — the one
arrangement already order-independent. It passed while the bug was live.

Mutation testing is necessary but not sufficient: it proves the check *can* fail, not that it
fails for the right reason.

### [CORRECTED] What is and is not gated

**a11y IS gated.** An earlier belief — repeated four times in one session and again by a fresh
analysis this week — was that a11y is ungated because there is no `.storybook/test-runner.js`.
**That is Storybook 8 knowledge and is wrong for what is installed.**
`@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4`'s `dist/setup-page-script.js:390-397` reads
`story.parameters?.a11y?.test` and throws when it `=== "error"`; `.storybook/preview.tsx:44`

Honest rider: the gate has never been made to fail on purpose, so by the standard above it is
**unproven, not absent**.

**Gated nowhere at all:** `eslint`, `prettier`, `tsc --noEmit`, `audit:tokens`, any CSS bundle
budget, test coverage. `npm run lint` currently fails repo-wide on pre-existing prettier errors
and CI never notices.

**A skipped required check counts as passing.** Live on PR #59: all four suites reported

`since_last_remote_commit`, and a final push touching only registry files fell outside every
allow-list. A 93-commit PR became merge-eligible with **zero test evidence on its head SHA**.

**A named gate that cannot fail:** `npm run test:contracts` is `echo 'TODO…' && exit 0`, and

### Harness traps

- **`test-storybook` needs a *built* Storybook.** Dev-server runs made four mutation results
  uninterpretable.
- **Vitest does not run `play`.**
- **jsdom always provides `window`**, so an SSR branch needs `// @vitest-environment node`.
- **Every jsdom rect is 0** — layout assertions there are meaningless.
- **`ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest.** It imports the base SFCC icons barrel, whose top-level

  vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))
  ```

- **`@storybook/test` is not installed.** `testing.md:115` prescribes it; Storybook 10 moved it

### The gap no tool covers

Duplication and reuse. No tool detects "this is a second Button." Nothing catches a bare token
key used as a JSX prop. Nothing catches a layout defect. Nothing catches a component whose data
doesn't exist on the tier it ships to.

17	## 1. The Operating Principles
18	
19	### Static-first
20	
21	Props in, markup out. A component under `overrides/app/components/` receives its data and
22	renders it. It does not fetch.
23	
24	Mock data goes in the story — never a temporary fetch you intend to remove. A component that
25	owns its own data-fetching cannot be reused where the data arrives differently: SSR-prefetched,
26	mocked in Storybook, or composed by a parent that already has it.
27	
28	**The one exception**, and it is narrow: Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks
29	(`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called from any component, including a presentational leaf.
30	They read from a Provider mounted above the route tree, so they don't create the
31	SSR/Storybook/composition problem the rule exists to prevent. This covers content identical for
32	every consumer regardless of route — not anything that varies per page.
33	
34	⚠️ **Their no-Provider behaviour differs and it will bite you in tests.** `useUiCopy` degrades
35	to fallback text and renders with zero setup. **`useIntl` throws**, and its `IntlProvider` is
36	mounted by the base SFCC `_app`, not `_app-config` — a narrower subtree than you'd expect. Any
37	Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer must wrap it.
38	
39	### Leverage what already exists
40	
41	Four rungs, in order:
42	
43	1. **Use the base SFCC component as-is.**
44	2. **Override it** — mirror the path under `overrides/`, keep the kebab-case filename.
45	
46	**The default is override, not build — because an override inherits the wiring for free.**
47	Override `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the
48	add-to-cart modal, bundle handling and `updateCart` already connected. And because the
49	resolver rewires imports transparently, overriding a component that SFCC's own base components
50	import means **the entire base template inherits your version with zero call sites touched**.
51	
52	Worked examples: size selector → `swatch-group`; add to bag → `product-view`; max quantity →
53	`quantity-picker`; variant resolution → `use-controlled-variations` / `use-derived-product`.
54	Check what the base already does before scoping — a ticket saying "Cart API integration is in
55	scope" may be describing a call the base already makes.
56	3. **Compose existing ui-kit atoms** into something new.
57	4. **Build a new component.** Rarest. Justify it.
58	
59	Before rung 4, check the registry (`.claude/registry/`) and grep `ui-kits/`.
60	
61	**What `shared/ui` is actually for:** Contentful renderers need *primitives*, not commerce
62	components. Every Contentful component on `develop` already pulls them in — `duplexSection`
63	(`Box`, `Text`), `collectionHero` (`Box`, `Button`, `Heading`, `Text`), `hotspotPopup`,
64	`imageText`, `heroBanner`. Upstream those resolve to bare Chakra.
65	
66	⚠️ **But the barrel is not the leverage play it looks like.** Overriding
67	`shared/ui/<Name>` to propagate branded styling into base cart/checkout/account **does not
68	work** — `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` re-exports relatively, which the resolver doesn't rewrite,
69	and 212 base files import the barrel (195 excluding tests) while **0** import the individual module. See
70	`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §4.

75	stale link propagates: you build the wrong thing, the BA signs off against a different frame,

79	There are **two Figma files** and cross-comparing them produces confident nonsense. See

88	The SOW allows **10 defects, no Sev3** — the whole project, not per sprint. (Contract figure;

95	## 2. Before you write any code
96	
97	### Confirm the branch
98	
99	```bash
100	git branch --show-current
101	```
102	
103	If it's `develop` or `main`, stop. No changes.
104	
105	### Check what already exists
106	
107	Read `.claude/registry/` for the component. The `Origin` column is what matters:
108	
109	| Origin | Means |
110	|---|---|
111	| `Custom` | Zimmermann-authored, already here |
112	| `Override` | already mirrored into `overrides/` |
113	| **`Base`** | **still upstream — you pay copy-first** |
114	
115	⚠️ **Do not trust the registry's `Tier` column.** `generateRegistry.mjs:125-203` hardcodes tier
116	arrays, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything else to Tier 4. Paths are reliable;
117	tiers are not. For what actually blocks, read `CODEOWNERS`.
118	
119	### The three component families
120	
121	| Family | Casing | Example |
122	|---|---|---|
123	| SFCC override | kebab-case, matching upstream exactly | `product-tile/` |
124	| **ui-kit component** | **camelCase — the default for new work** | `zimmButton/` |
125	| `shared/ui` primitive | PascalCase, mirroring upstream | `Button/` |
126	
127	Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Naming a Zimmermann-
128	authored file in kebab-case falsely signals Salesforce origin — which inverts the convention's
129	whole purpose.
130	
131	### Where a new component goes
132	
133	```
134	overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/
135	  index.tsx
136	  index.stories.tsx
137	  <name>.css.ts          ← the recipe
138	  index.test.tsx         ← if it has branching or event wiring
139	```
140	
141	**Tier by composition, read off the imports:**
142	
143	- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit
144	- **molecule** — composes atoms, light local state
145	- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**
146	
147	An icon passed as a prop doesn't count. Slotted children don't count.
148	
149	### What's actually overridden today
150	
151	Eleven directories:
152	
153	```
154	_app-config  button  contentful  footer  foundation  header
155	icons  pageContainer  product-view  ui-kits  uiCopyProvider
156	```
157	
158	Still base, despite being referenced throughout `.claude/rules/`: `product-tile`,
159	`display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `list-menu`, `drawer-menu`, `seo`.
160	**Assume most stories pay copy-first.**
161	
162	### The copy-first rule
163	
164	For any task requiring an override that doesn't exist yet, prepare **all of them at once**
165	before any functional change:
166	
167	1. Copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path.
168	2. Convert to `.ts`/`.tsx`, update imports.
169	3. `npx tsc --noEmit`.
170	4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` to each.
171	5. **Stop.** Let the user confirm the overrides are rendering.
172	6. Remove the `console.log`s, then make functional changes.
173	
174	Never bundle this silently with functional work.
