file.content: # FED Lead Playbook **Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 · **Revised:** 25 August 2026 The lead role: what you say, to whom, and when. Judgement and process, not procedure. **Companions:** `fedBuild-manual.md` (how to build a component) · `uiBuild-knowledge.md` (why the machine behaves the way it does). **Authority on styling:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`. If this file disagrees with it, that file wins. *This document absorbed `zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md` (retired 25 Aug 2026). Its durable operating principles are §3; its training-vehicle material — a Next.js/Tailwind stack that isn't this one — was dropped.* --- ## 1. The mandate Sixteen responsibilities landed across two Contentful-vs-PWA-Kit alignment meetings. They reduce to two mandates: - **M1 — Protect the build.** Reuse, conventions, review, accessibility, performance. - **M2 — Protect the plan.** Estimation, scope, dependencies, escalation. **The one to resist as stated:** being a serial refinement gate across both squads. It won't scale and it will slip. Name that rather than absorbing it — an unresourced ask that quietly becomes yours is the failure mode here. ### The quality bar this serves The SOW allows **10 defects, no Sev3**, for the whole project. (Contract figure — nothing in `.docs/` records it, so cite the SOW itself, not the repo.) Three consequences: 1. **Vigilance is the job**, not an overhead on it. 2. **Budget real time per UI PR** — an hour or more. That's the cost of the review, not slippage. 3. **Flag rather than invent.** A guessed value that ships is a defect with your name on it. --- ## 2. Operating rhythm | Moment | Plays | |---|---| | Story drafting | 1, 3, 4 | | Refinement | 1, 2, 8 | | Pre-sprint planning | 2, 8 | | PR review | 5, 5b, 6 | | Weekly design review | 9 | --- ## 3. Principles *Absorbed from the retired playbook. These are the parts that survived contact with the codebase.* ### The quality ceiling is set by the human An AI assistant has no standards of its own — the standards and the constraints are things you supply. Its real value is making your assumptions visible faster, not making decisions. ### The dual mandate You hold two hats and the failure mode is collapsing into one. | | IC | Lead | |---|---|---| | Think | about the component | about the system | | Ask | until the spec is unambiguous | until the *team's* spec is unambiguous | | Decide | how to build it | whether it should be built now | | Review | your own output hardest | the pattern, not the line | | Protect | the build | the plan | | Multiply | — | the highest-leverage thing you do | **IC drift:** you're the only one who knows how something works. **Lead drift:** you haven't written code in a week and your review comments are getting vaguer. ### Defeating agreeableness An assistant that agrees with you is worth nothing. Four techniques that work: - **Role framing** — "you are a reviewer whose job is to find what's wrong with this." - **Steelman** — "give me the strongest argument *against* this approach." - **Critique-first** — ask for the problems before asking for the solution. - **Constraint injection** — name the constraint it must satisfy, so it can't hand-wave. Make it a team norm, not a private trick. ### Polishing is procrastination If an edit to a rules file didn't change what someone can or can't do, it wasn't a real edit. ### Define done, or nothing stops This applies to people and tools equally. "Improve the footer" has no terminal state. --- ## 4. Working with AI tooling *New section. The expensive failures on this project were not bad code — they were unrequested work and unrequested commits.* ### The authorisation ladder — three separate levels **Investigate ≠ fix ≠ commit.** "Run it" and "have a look" are investigation requests. They are not approval to change code, and changing code is not approval to commit it. Correct shape: **change → verify → stop and show the diff → wait.** This sharpens AGENTS.md Hard Rule #15 with the distinction the rule leaves implicit. Resuming from a session summary, a task list, or a "natural next step" is **not** an instruction to commit. ### The audit-loop failure mode A build can become a self-sustaining audit-and-fix cycle that feels productive and isn't. Measured on one stretch of SFCC-55: **55 commits, a 3.0:1 rework ratio, `footer/index.tsx` touched 32 times in 5 days.** The work wasn't wasted — it was mis-ordered. **The diagnostic that separates real work from generated work:** where did the finding come from? Six findings fixed things that were actually broken. Seven came from *reading code we'd just written*. If a finding's origin is your own fresh output rather than a spec, a reproduced failure, or a review comment, it is probably not the next thing to do. Two correctives: - **Read the review queue before starting a self-directed pass.** A six-hour-old Major finding named a live security bypass while the loop was polishing comment placement. - **Ban "it's good practice" as a justification.** A fix needs a named requirement, a reproduced failure, or a review comment behind it. ### Present verdicts, don't auto-fix When a pass produces a list of possible improvements, separate the ones traceable to a spec/failure/review from the ones traceable to your own just-written code — and **offer** the second group rather than doing them. ### Don't take an agent's report at face value Two agent claims were overturned by direct verification in a single session this week: that a11y is ungated (it is gated — the agent was reasoning from Storybook 8), and that the CLI would work with the repo's management token (it reads neither that env var nor any other). Both were confidently stated and internally coherent. **The check is cheap; the propagation cost is not** — a wrong claim in a doc gets cited for months. ### Local-only docs stay local These three files live on this machine. **Never cite them in a PR reply, a commit message, or a code comment.** A citation nobody else can open reads as an appeal to a private authority, and for CodeRabbit specifically it teaches the bot nothing. When a local doc is the real reason for a decision, find the public equivalent in `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/rules/` or `.docs/` and cite that. If none exists, argue the merits directly. No `Co-Authored-By` trailer on commits. --- ### Shipping discipline Fixed-price clock, 10-defect budget. Four rules that follow from that: - **Deploy first.** A thing that runs somewhere other than your machine is the only evidence that counts. - **Partial-but-hardened beats complete-but-broken.** Three states done properly ships; six states half-wired doesn't. - **Descope, never cut quality.** Cutting the loading state to hit a date converts a schedule problem into a defect-budget problem, and the budget is smaller. - **The 20-minute rule.** Twenty minutes without progress is a signal to change approach or ask, not to push harder. ### Three states are AC, not polish Every component that renders fetched data needs **loading** (a skeleton, not a spinner), **error** (with retry), and **absent** (see `uiBuild-knowledge.md` §7) specified in the story. If they aren't in the AC they won't be built, and they're where the defects come from. Related tell: an **invented data source** is a story problem, not a code problem — fix the story. And an over-engineering tell worth naming: a component estimated at 25–35 lines coming back as 120. ### Review culture The PR mechanics are §Play 5. The culture is this: - **Regroup every work block**, not just at sprint boundaries. - **Learn from the work, don't judge the person.** A review that makes someone defensive costs more than the defect it found. - **Rotate who's on screen.** The person driving learns most; it shouldn't always be you. - **The showcase is honest, not polished.** Demo the real state. - **Commitments are specific enough to check.** "I'll look at it" isn't one. ### The corrections-to-rules loop **The highest-leverage question you can ask at the end of a work block:** *where did the tooling make a decision I didn't specify — and what would I add to the AC or the rules to prevent that next time?* A correction you make once and forget is a correction you'll make fifty times. And test each candidate rule against: **is this something that can be checked against, or an aspiration that will be ignored?** Second question, equally cheap: **"is that gap fixed now, or did you just acknowledge it?"** Acknowledgement reads like resolution and isn't. ## Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check Four rungs: use as-is → override → compose existing atoms → build new. Rung 4 is rarest and needs justification. **Where to look:** `.claude/registry/` for `Origin` (`Custom` / `Override` / **`Base`**), then `ui-kits/`. ⚠️ The registry's `Tier` column is unreliable — `generateRegistry.mjs:125-203` hardcodes tiers, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything to Tier 4. **`Origin = Base` is the hidden cost.** It means copy-first: mirror the file, convert to TS, verify the override renders, *then* build. That's real effort and it belongs in the estimate. Eight components referenced throughout `.claude/rules/` are still base. **The `shared/ui` barrel exception.** Overriding `shared/ui/` to propagate styling into base cart/checkout/account looks like enormous leverage. It intercepts nothing — the barrel re-exports relatively, which the resolver doesn't rewrite, and 212 base files import the barrel (195 excluding tests) while **0** import the individual module. Don't scope a story around it. **Duplicate atoms are a human problem.** No tool detects "this is a second Button." The fix that makes it self-service is one line in the BA's story template: *name the component, and state whether it exists.* ### The atoms governance model — decided ``` overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}// ``` Tier by composition (what the component's own template renders), camelCase for Zimmermann-authored, a registered recipe always. ⚠️ **The rules set is split on this.** `components.md` and `conventions.md` contain **zero** occurrences of `ui-kits`, `atoms`, `molecules` or `organisms`. `new-component/SKILL.md:29` still scaffolds to the flat path. `.docs/architecture.md` contradicts itself. Reconciling this is a standing item. --- ## Play 2 — Estimation validation **The re-baseline to say once:** pages go *down*, components go *up by more*. Component-based decomposition front-loads the work. Split component-build effort from page-composition effort in every estimate. They have different risk profiles and different owners. Challenge list: 1. Is it `Origin = Base`? Add copy-first. 2. Does it exist in `ui-kits` already? 3. Is a Contentful content type needed? That's a second story. 4. Is the Figma frame signed off, or "Not Confirmed"? 5. Does it depend on an integration that isn't wired? Most aren't. 6. Does its data exist on the tiers it must demo on? 7. Is it multi-site? Eight storefronts, eleven locales, by default. --- ## Play 3 — Component completeness & variant review **Configuration variant** (a prop) vs **composition variant** (a container or slot — structurally a second component). Getting this wrong at story time produces a component that can't express what the design needs. ⚠️ **Contentful sync is additive-only**, so a variant modelled wrongly is semi-permanent. Field deletion is opt-in (`--delete-deleted-fields`) and off by default, deliberately. Optional fields need explicit AC for the absent case — see the three-tier absent-data policy in `uiBuild-knowledge.md` §7. --- ## Play 4 — The renderer contract One field-ID table, **identical in both stories** of a Contentful pair. You own the template, the BA fills it, you sign off the field IDs. | Field ID | Type | Required | Localised | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | `image` | Media | yes | no | | | `imageAlt` | Short text | yes | yes | empty string permitted for decorative | | `bodyCopy` | Rich text | no | yes | absent case must render perceivably | | `ctaLabel` | Short text | no | yes | required if `ctaUrl` set | | `ctaUrl` | Short text | no | no | passes `isSafeHref`; external links get the 3.2.5 suffix | **Field IDs, not display names.** "Body copy" in prose is where drift starts. The IDs are the contract — a rename after authoring begins is a migration, not an edit. Requirement source is `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §2. ⚠️ **Studio Experiences inverts the order** — the contract is generated from the React props rather than authored first, so the review point moves to the component's prop type. --- ## Play 5 — PR review ### Already mechanical — don't spend review time here Conventional commit format · registry regeneration · derived-config edit blocking · `.env.sample` secret shapes · tag naming · the two `semgrep.yml` security rules (unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, payment-credential logging) · the three ast-grep a11y rules (`warning` only) · Storybook a11y (`preview.tsx` sets `a11y.test: 'error'`; the installed test-runner enforces it). ⚠️ By Play 5b's own standard the a11y gate is **unproven** — it has never been made to fail on purpose. It's on this list because it runs, not because it's been demonstrated to catch anything. Worth one deliberate break to find out. ### Gate zero — does it build ⚠️ **Read the check *history*, not the head SHA.** `detect-changes` diffs `since_last_remote_commit`, so a docs-only final commit flips both required checks green even if an earlier push failed them. **A skipped required check counts as passing.** PR #59 merged with all four suites `skipping` and zero test evidence on its head SHA. Also: `Playwright E2E (localhost)` and `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)` are **required nowhere** — they can be red and the PR merges. ### Review across three surfaces 1. **The diff** — tokens, naming, dead code, test coverage. 2. **The preview environment** — every `feature/**`/`fix/**` push (except `fix/release-*`) gets its own MRT URL. 3. **Figma, side by side**, mobile *and* desktop. Layout defects are invisible in a diff and invisible to every automated gate. `width: 'xl'` resolving to 576px destroyed the footer on every page while passing `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`, CodeRabbit twice, and the a11y run. ### The token checklist - Bare token key on a **sizing** or **typography** prop → wrong or dropped silently - Bare token string where `var(--zimm-*)` is now required - Raw hex/px/rem/em without a `provisional`/`pending`/`audit-allow` comment - Recipe not namespaced → silent deep-merge into a base SFCC recipe - Recipe not registered → runtime throw - Compound value (`padding: 'xs 0'`) → emitted verbatim, dropped ### Tests and stories — the minimum A story for anything exported. A test where there's branching or event wiring. Resolve duplicate coverage by **scoping what the test asserts** — mock the child whose internals are proven elsewhere — not by leaving the component with no test of its own. ### Ten questions, in order 1. Does it build, and did the checks actually *run*? 2. Does it match Figma at both breakpoints? 3. Is anything here already in `ui-kits`? 4. Any raw design value? 5. Any bare token key on a sizing/typography prop? 6. Is the recipe namespaced and registered? 7. Keyboard operable, focus visible, names on controls, 24×24 targets? 8. Does the absent-data case render something perceivable? 9. Does its data exist on the tiers it must demo on? 10. Does the protection-tier block in the PR body match the actual diff? --- ## Play 5b — Verifying a claim before you act on it *Learned expensively. Reversals here would each have shipped a wrong change.* - **Absence in an extracted spec is not a decision.** A field missing from a Figma export may mean "not specified" or "deliberately none" — those are different, and you can't tell from the absence. - **A codebase value isn't a spec until you find its source.** Someone typed it. Find out who and why before treating it as intent. - **Ask for the node.** A Figma *screenshot* in a ticket is not the frame. Node type decides whether a measurement is even comparable. - **Value-matching audits produce confident nonsense.** "These 41 literals should be tokens" inflated from 19 by matching `.rem` inside `removeEventListener`. - **A grep count is not a coverage verdict.** When a count returns zero, establish *which* zero: untested, tested elsewhere, or unused. - **A passing test can encode the bug.** A tie-break suite named "order doesn't change the outcome" used only distinct timestamps — the one arrangement already order-independent. It passed while the bug was live. **The shape all of these share: a proxy reported as the finding.** The standard: **make the check fail on purpose before its pass counts.** If something is asserted rather than proven, say so. --- ## Play 6 — Accessibility WCAG **2.2** AA. Per-component AC: keyboard operable · visible focus · accessible name · correct semantic element · contrast 4.5:1 / 3:1 · **24×24 target size** (2.5.8, a 2.2 addition). **What the tooling misses**, so don't treat a clean run as clearance: the `` ast-grep rule matches `^img$` only and is blind to Chakra's ``; the `IconButton` rule rejects `aria-labelledby` — the more correct answer — because of a word-boundary bug; the clickable-non-interactive rule checks neither `tabIndex` nor `onKeyDown`. All three are `severity: warning`. **Open item:** whether missing alt text should be absent or `alt=""` is a content-model question, not a code one. Needs a decision from Tim. --- ## Play 7 — Page-level validation | Part | Where it lands today | |---|---| | E2E | partial — **one spec file exists in the entire repo** | | Lighthouse | yes, at SIT tier | | **Design parity** | **no automated home — defaults to you** | ⚠️ **No page has a Storybook story**, despite `components.md` requiring one for page-level assemblies. The `@area` vocabulary is `homepage · checkout · search · account · pdp · plp · integrations`. Only `homepage` has a spec, and only `e2e_homepage` is mapped in the change-scoping config — each new area's first spec needs its own allow-list group or it silently falls back to the full suite. Visual regression (Chromatic / Loki / Percy) would give design parity an automated home. It's a new dependency and a budget line, so it needs approval before it's proposed as a plan. --- ## Play 8 — Pushing back before sizing **The Figma link on the card is a build input.** A stale link propagates three ways: the dev builds the wrong thing, the BA signs off against a different frame, QA tests a third source. Ask the BA to fix the card. **Decisions need a findable home.** A decision recorded only in a Teams thread will be re-litigated within a month. ### The product-side register — live, decision-blocking | Open item | Position to hold | |---|---| | **Recommendations** | `SFCC-7` already holds eight decomposed tickets, and **SFCC-647 is `Ready for Development`** and answers the data-source question. Raise 647 — don't create tickets. | | **Shop the Look naming** | Four names for possibly two things: "Shop the Look" (SFCC-90), "Shop the Edit" (SFCC-313), "Product Cards with Lookbook" (04.7), and `shoppableImage`, which already exists in code. Force one name before either is estimated. | | **Preview & publishing** | The preview token is set on dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging/prod. Both preview paths 404 without it and are `noindex`. **Authors preview on `uat`.** "Can we preview on prod?" needs a Tier 1 change against a documented security rationale. | | **Contentful pattern per component** | Entry-driven vs Studio Experiences. **Highest-value item to close** — it decides story order and whether the incremental-assembly loop is even available. | | **`regions` content-model field** | Unconfirmed, and it affects every Contentful component's variant model across eight storefronts. | | **Composed-page ownership** | "Not product/category → Contentful" doesn't settle PDP/PLP editorial blocks or category landing pages. **Category landing pages are the sharp edge, and PLP work is already in flight.** | --- ## Play 9 — Design-system escalation Standing route for missing tokens: the weekly design review. Live gaps: - **Button has no Colour axis.** The 04.7 spec says "Normal, Inverse"; the implementation exposes only `variant` + `size`. The registry reports **10 consumers**, so adding the axis later touches ten call sites. - **Icon Button is marked Done in 04.7 and has no implementation at all.** - `zimmButton`'s provisional heights (50px/41px) disagree with Handover's `actionSizes` (52px/40px); `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no token at all. - **`textStyles.navigation`** is the only one of 22 hardcoding `lineHeight: 'normal'`; Figma reportedly specifies 100%. - **Spacing gaps** — 28px and 44px are in use with no named entry between `xl` (24) and `2xl` (32), or `3xl` (40) and `4xl` (64). - Primary-button hover fails AA at **2.96:1**; there's no inverse focus-ring token. ⚠️ **"Done" in the 04.7 component tracker means design-confirmed, not API-matched.** Those are different states and the tracker doesn't distinguish them. **What to do when the design system itself is wrong** — e.g. a token that fails the project's own WCAG 2.2 AA target — is unresolved. Someone has to accept that risk explicitly; right now nobody has. --- ## Governance — what actually blocks *Expanded. PREDICATE: No JSX prop or recipe key in `width`, `height`, `boxSize`, `minWidth/maxWidth`, `minHeight/maxHeight` has a bare string scale key (`'xl'`, `'m'`, `'s'`, `'l'`, `'2xl'`…). It must be `var(--zimm-scale-*)` or an explicit unit value.

PREDICATE: No `fontSize`, `lineHeight` or `letterSpacing` anywhere in the diff carries a bare token key; typography is expressed via `textStyle` or an explicit `var(--zimm-*)` / unit value.

## SECTION C — INTERNAL DISAGREEMENTS AND TWO-WAY READINGS

**C1 — Is `var(--zimm-*)` in JSX required, or is any design value in JSX itself the violation?**
Reading A: the hierarchy was corrected so that raw CSS-custom-property references in JSX are now the *required* form; a bare token string is the finding and the fix is to rewrite it as `var()`. Reading B: the same sections state brand values mostly should not be in JSX at all, that `var()` in JSX is for a genuine prop-system gap only, and that the measured reality is exactly one such instance — under which reading a `var()` in JSX is itself a finding and the fix is to move the value into the recipe. The two named live violations (`color="text.default"` in two atoms) get different remedies depending on which reading applies. SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — [CORRECTED]; fedBuild §3 — [CORRECTED] Rung 2 inverted

**C2 — Is recipe co-location neutral, preferred, or a governance smell?**
Reading A: purely organisational — Chakra resolves by string key, so co-located or central is a free choice. Reading B: the folder layout and quick reference both prescribe a co-located `<name>.css.ts` as the standard shape. Reading C: co-location is a governance hazard, because the last-match-wins CODEOWNERS rule for `**/*.css.ts` silently drops the Tier 2 approver requirement that the surrounding directory carries — flagged as something nothing prevents for `_app-config/` or `seo/`. SOURCE: uiBuild §3 — Styling surface / Co-location changes who reviews it; fedBuild §2, §13; fedLead — Last-match-wins

**C3 — 14 recipe files or 18?**
One doc measures `var(--zimm-*)` in 14 theme files on `develop` (10 co-located + 4 central), with 18 only in the uncommitted working tree. The other states 18 recipe files measured on `develop`. Both cite the same date and commit. An auditor using either as a baseline will get a different delta. SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — What survives from the old advice; fedBuild §3 — In practice this rarely arises

**C4 — Is `.scss` a permitted last resort or prohibited?**
Reading A: scoped `.scss` is rung 5 of the styling hierarchy — legitimate when `sx` genuinely cannot express something, with the rider "in practice: never". Reading B: styling is a registered recipe, always — explicitly not a plain stylesheet, with a structural argument (a stylesheet can only see the derived output at the bottom of the pipeline). SOURCE: fedBuild §3 — The styling hierarchy; uiBuild §3 — Styling surface

**C5 — Which vehicle expresses a prop-system gap: `sx`, or a JSX prop with `var()`?**
The hierarchy names `sx` as rung 4 for a one-off gap. The single sanctioned real-world instance is a conditional `paddingLeft` written as a JSX prop, not as `sx`. Whether a reviewer should require the gap to be expressed as `sx` or as a `var()`-valued prop is unstated, and the docs model each. SOURCE: fedBuild §3 — The styling hierarchy; uiBuild §1 — What survives from the old advice

**C6 — Tier is read off the imports, or off what the template renders?**
Reading A: read it off the imports, not the DOM. Reading B: tier by composition meaning what the component's own template renders. These diverge for a component that imports nothing but renders slotted ui-kit children, and for one that imports a ui-kit component it renders only conditionally. SOURCE: uiBuild §3 — Tier is by composition; fedLead Play 1 — The atoms governance model

**C7 — Is a11y covered by CI or is it manual-review territory?**
All three docs correct the earlier claim and state the a11y gate exists and runs. Two of them add, in the same breath, that it has never been made to fail on purpose and is therefore unproven, and one lists it under "already mechanical — don't spend review time here" while simultaneously recommending a deliberate break to find out whether it works. An auditor can reasonably treat a11y as gated (skip it) or as unverified (test it manually). SOURCE: uiBuild §10 — [CORRECTED] What is and is not gated; fedBuild §6 — [CORRECTED]; fedLead Play 5

**C8 — Is `alt=""` for decorative images settled or an open decision?**
Reading A: settled — `alt=""` for decorative is stated as the rule in the a11y patterns, the build manual's ast-grep section, and the renderer-contract field table (empty string permitted for decorative). Reading B: explicitly open — whether missing alt text should be *absent* or `alt=""` is named as a content-model question awaiting a decision from a named person. SOURCE: uiBuild §9; fedBuild §6; fedLead Play 4 vs fedLead Play 6 — Open item

**C9 — Does the shared Contentful hook hardcode `include`, or accept it?**
One doc says the shared hook builds a URL with `content_type`, `access_token` and `include`, implying a caller-supplied depth. The other says the footer passes `include: 3` *where the shared hook hardcodes `include=2`* — which cannot both be true of the same call path. Whether a new consumer can raise its own depth, or must work around a hardcoded 2, is undetermined. SOURCE: uiBuild §8 — Fetch-depth / Locale is not passed; fedBuild §7 — Fetch depth is load-bearing

**C10 — Is the static-content-hook exception a closed list or a category?**
The exception is phrased as "Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks" with `useIntl` and `useUiCopy` in parentheses. Reading A: those two hooks only. Reading B: any hook meeting the stated criteria (Provider above the route tree, content identical for every consumer regardless of route) qualifies. An auditor will accept or reject a third such hook differently. SOURCE: uiBuild §3 — One documented exception; fedBuild §1 — The one exception

**C11 — Who owns loading and error state?**
Reading A: components under `components/` receive data as props and do not fetch — so loading/error belong to the page or container. Reading B: every component that renders fetched data needs loading, error and absent states specified. A presentational leaf cannot know it is loading unless a prop tells it, and the docs don't say which layer holds the state. SOURCE: fedBuild §1 — Static-first; uiBuild §3; fedLead §3 — Three states are AC

**C12 — Do pages need Storybook stories?**
Reading A: every component exported from its folder needs a story; `Pages/` is one of the seven story categories, implying page-level stories are expected. Reading B: no page has a story today, despite a rules file requiring one for page-level assemblies — recorded as a live gap, not as a branch-blocking requirement. A page-and-components branch is affected directly. SOURCE: fedBuild §5 — Storybook / Categorisation; fedLead Play 7

**C13 — Do directly-imported foundation constants violate the no-design-values-in-JSX principle?**
`iconSizes`, `actionSizes` and `motion` are prescribed as imported constants used directly in JSX props (`boxSize={iconSizes.lg}`), which places a resolved design value in JSX and bypasses `var()` entirely. Reading A: a sanctioned exception, because these deliberately are not registered scales. Reading B: an inconsistency with both the "brand values shouldn't be in JSX" principle and the `var()` requirement, which the docs do not reconcile. Reading B: any consumption of a provisional value should carry the acknowledgement comment at the point of use. The camelCase rule is stated as applying to all Zimmermann-authored directories, with kebab-case reserved for files mirroring Salesforce. `ui-kits` itself is kebab-cased and is explicitly named as an undocumented, unsettled exception, with a warning that leaving it undocumented invites further kebab directories.
